ideas.name: ClaspChronicle
ideas.niche: Visual era identification for antique hardware
ideas.problem: Inability to quickly and accurately identify the historical era of small hardware, leading to improper restoration choices or undervalued antique sales.
ideas.targetUser: DIY home restorers, professional antique dealers, and estate sale hunters (ages 25–65) seeking rapid authentication of small metal components.
coreFeatures: AI-Powered Instant Era Scanner
Historical Style & Material Encyclopedia
Restoration & Cleaning Intelligence Guides
Digital Provenance Vault for Collection Tracking
realDependencies: TensorFlow or Google Cloud Vision API for image classification
Relational Database (PostgreSQL) for historical era metadata
AWS S3 for hosting user-captured hardware galleries
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON manifest containing pre-defined 'hardware profiles' (e.g., 'Victorian Brass Latch', 'Mid-Century Chrome Hinge'). When the user triggers a scan, the app will trigger a 2.5-second 'Processing' overlay with a simulated scanning line animation. The system will use a randomized lookup function to pick a profile from the manifest, returning a result with a fake 'Confidence Score' (between 85% and 99%) and matching metadata. To simulate network latency, all 'API' calls will be wrapped in a Promise that resolves after a variable delay of 1500ms to 3000ms.

ideas.name: SpoolScout
ideas.niche: Rapid filament depletion estimation for 3D printing
ideas.problem: The 'mid-print failure' caused by running out of filament due to inaccurate estimations of remaining material weight versus project requirements.
ideas.targetUser: Hobbyist and prosumer 3D printing makers who run long-duration prints (10+ hours) and want a low-friction way to validate spool capacity without managing complex inventory databases.
coreFeatures: Quick-Entry Weight Input (Current Spool Weight - Tare/Core Weight)
Material Density Presets (PLA, PETG, ABS, TPU, etc. to auto-calculate mass/volume)
Project Matchmaker (Input project grams/time to get a 'Will it Finish?' status)
Visual Safety Gauges (Green/Yellow/Red color-coded status indicators for remaining print time)
realDependencies: Cloud database (e.g., Firebase) for user-saved spool/material profiles
Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) API for integration with smart scales or smart spooling hardware
External material science database for precise polymer density values
ideas.emulationStrategy: Simulate network latency using a 800ms delay on all 'Save' and 'Load' actions. Use a local JSON manifest to mimic a cloud database for user profiles. Instead of real BLE hardware, implement a 'Simulated Scale' slider component that injects weight values into the app state. Replace the material science API with a hardcoded lookup object that returns density values after a brief, randomized loading state.

ideas.name: FitCompass
ideas.niche: Global apparel size-mapping and brand-specific fit standardization
ideas.problem: Inconsistent international sizing standards and brand-to-brand variance lead to high e-commerce return rates and consumer frustration during cross-border shopping.
ideas.targetUser: Tech-savvy Gen Z and Millennial global shoppers, frequent international travelers, and expatriates who frequently purchase from non-domestic e-commerce platforms.
coreFeatures: Universal Sizing Engine: Instant conversion between JP, EU, UK, US, and AU standards.
Personal Brand-Fit Vault: A digital profile storing 'true fit' history for specific brands to account for cut and silhouette variance.
AI Garment Scanner: Uses computer vision to extract precise measurements from a photo of a user's best-fitting item.
Smart Shopping Overlay: A mobile-optimized view that overlays recommended sizes directly onto product sizing charts.
realDependencies: Computer Vision API (e.g., Google ML Kit) for garment dimension extraction
E-commerce Product Data APIs (e.g., Shopify, Amazon) to fetch real-time size charts
Cloud-based User Profile Database (e.g., Firebase/AWS) for storing fit history
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local JSON manifest containing mock size charts for 100 diverse brands. To simulate AI scanning, the app will trigger a 3-second 'Processing...' animation with a progress bar, ultimately returning randomized dimensions within a realistic ±0.5cm range of a preset user profile. API calls to brand databases will be mimicked using asynchronous functions with a 1.5-second artificial latency to simulate network round-trips. The browser extension feature will be emulated via a dedicated 'Mock Storefront' view within the app that simulates a live web page environment.

ideas.name: WattWise
ideas.niche: Electrical safety monitoring for smart home IoT ecosystems.
ideas.problem: The risk of electrical fires and device failure caused by overloading low-cost, unmonitored smart plugs and power strips in increasingly complex smart home setups.
ideas.targetUser: Tech-savvy smart home enthusiasts, apartment renters in older buildings, and DIY home automation users (ages 25-45) who frequently add new IoT devices to existing power configurations.
coreFeatures: Appliance Wattage Library: A searchable database of common household electronics and their average power draws.
Cumulative Load Calculator: An additive interface allowing users to 'stack' devices to see total projected wattage.
Safety Capacity Gauge: A real-time visual indicator (Green/Yellow/Red) showing how close a specific plug is to its maximum rated load.
Smart Plug Profiler: A quick-select menu for popular smart plug brands and models to automatically set the safety ceiling.
realDependencies: IoT Manufacturer APIs (e.g., TP-Link Kasa, Wemo, or Tuya) to pull real-time power consumption
Matter/Thread protocol integration for cross-brand device communication
Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) for critical safety alerts
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will replace live API calls with a local JSON 'World State' containing 50 common appliances and 10 smart plug models with fixed wattage limits. To simulate real-time electricity monitoring, a setInterval function will apply a random jitter (±3-5% fluctuation) to the 'current load' values. Every 'Search' or 'Connect' action will be wrapped in a Promise with a randomized 800ms to 1800ms delay to simulate network latency. If a user adds a device that pushes the total wattage above the mock plug's limit, a locally triggered UI event will simulate a high-priority push notification.

ideas.name: ProfilePilot
ideas.problem: The high risk of purchasing expensive custom keycap sets that do not match a user's keyboard layout (e.g., missing 1.75u Shift or 1u Alt keys) or physical stem type (e.g., MX vs. Choc).
ideas.targetUser: Mechanical keyboard hobbyists and custom builders (ages 18-45) who frequent enthusiast communities like r/MechanicalKeyboards and regularly invest in high-end, niche-specific keycap sets.
coreFeatures: Interactive Layout Mapper: A visual grid to define the user's specific keyboard size (60%, TKL, Alice, etc.) and ISO/ANSI configuration.
Profile Silhouette Visualizer: A side-view comparison tool that renders the height and slant differences between profiles like SA, Cherry, and OEM.
Modifier Matcher: A logic engine that flags missing or incorrectly sized modifier keys (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, etc.) within a selected set.
Stem Compatibility Check: A validator to ensure keycap stem types match the user's specific switch mounting system.
realDependencies: Vendor Product APIs (e.g., Drop, KBDFans, or GMK) to pull real-time set specifications
Comprehensive Keyboard Layout Database (covering ISO, ANSI, and JIS variations)
WebGL or Three.js for real-time 3D profile rendering
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON file containing a 'Mock Product Catalog' of 10 popular keycap sets with pre-defined dimensions and profiles. All 'API calls' will be wrapped in a function that utilizes a 1200ms setTimeout to simulate network latency. Instead of a true 3D engine, the profile visualizer will use 2D SVG path manipulations that scale vertically to represent different profile heights. A hardcoded rule engine will trigger 'Incompatibility Alerts' whenever a user selects a layout/set combination known to be problematic in the mock data (e.g., a 65% layout paired with a set lacking a 1.75u Shift key).
